## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0df9c8b2139f37f0b03bd7b1a328e1acf8bd2566`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md + none

Read for this review: card #32585 (body and its four comments), this PR's body, its file list (one file) and the net diff against the merge base `874166b6` (+137 / -7), and the 49 check-runs on the head. The code and records the amendment cites were read on `main` at `ac7b9d80`; none of those files differs between the merge base and that commit. Nothing was checked out, built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of `@objectstack/spec`: unchanged by this diff. Right.** The diff is ADR prose. `defineStack` accepts and refuses what it did on the merge base. The ADR says the module half of the rule is "declared and not yet enforced", and that agrees with `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts#validateSingleApp` (it returns nothing unless `manifest.type` is `app`) and with the `driver` pin in `packages/spec/src/stack.test.ts`.
- **A narrowing is declared, not shipped. Right.** A `type: module` package with two apps builds today and is to be refused. That refusal is #32586's diff and carries its own `Clause-②:` line there. This PR changes no accept-set.
- **The governed rule surface: D3 widens for a suite and keeps the limit per package. Right.** The rule paragraph equals card item 1 word for word. The one sentence added after it ("Read per package: no package of a suite defines more than one app") follows from "each app is defined by a different package of the suite".
- **No published docs surface moves. Right.** `docs/adr/**` ships in no package. `docs/adr/README.md` is not in the diff and needs no regeneration for this edit: its ADR-0019 row is built from the title, the `Date` line and the status cut short (`scripts/adr-index.mjs#statusCell`), and the cut falls before the first changed word. The new status text holds no "superseded", the word the Superseded-by column looks for on a status line. The index job in CI is report-only, so this is a reading, not a gate verdict.
- **New coupling: ten symbol anchors.** `appRoute.ts#appRouteSegment`, `#matchAppBySegment`, `#appAddressSegment`, `protocol-package-scope.ts#resolveAppPackageIdKey`, `stack.zod.ts#validateCrossReferences`, `#DefineStackOptions.artifactObjects`, `#validateSingleApp`, `app.zod.ts#requiresObject`, `packages.ts#isDisableableAppModule`, `protocol-authoring-refusals.ts#isItemOfDisabledPackage`. Each exists on `main` under that name. A rename of any of them now reds `check:adr-symbol-anchors`, which is the intended binding.
- **Runtime strings that cite D3 stay true under the amended text.** `validateSingleApp`'s refusal ("split into separate packages") and the warning in `resolveAppPackageIdKey` ("a package may define at most one app (ADR-0019 D3)") both read per package.

Gate verdicts are the check-runs on the head: 49 runs, 26 success, 23 skipped, none failed, none pending.

### ② Semver level

Nothing in the diff publishes. The PR carries `skip-changeset` and `Check Changeset` is green. The title has no `!`.

`Clause-②: no` on the PR body is right: no published schema is touched and no accept-set moves in this diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` in the dev report is empty. The dev's flags, each answered:

- **Line citations written as symbol anchors.** Answered. The three `appRoute.ts` symbols are what the card's line range covers on `main`, read here.
- **HotCRM not opened; `hotcrm:src/sales/apps/crm.app.ts` and the hotcrm plan (M11) are cited on the card's word.** Answered, and it stays a flag for the maintainer's read. The ADR attributes both in its own text ("#32585 cites HotCRM's sales app for it", "The hotcrm plan builds on it"), so it asserts no reading of that repository. This review did not open hotcrm either: it is outside the review's inputs.
- **Reason 2 has an exception the card does not state (`requiresObject`).** Answered: it is real, read at the navigation walk in `validateCrossReferences`. The cited function has a second one. See F1.
- **Anchors added to reasons 1 and 3.** Answered: each was read and holds (④).
- **Text written beyond card items 1 to 4** (reversed and stands, enforced and not yet, not decided, the readings of ADR-0130 D2 and ADR-0141, the notes under Context, D4, Scope and Consequences, Alternatives entry 4, one References line). Answered: none adds a rule the ruling does not carry. Two are inferences the maintainer should see, and the PR body points at both: ADR-0130 D2's "exactly one consumer-visible consequence" gains a second, and alternative 1's rejection is narrowed.
- **`docs/adr/README.md` untouched.** Answered by the reading under ①: the row does not move.
- **Out of scope, noted and not filed: ADR-0130 (D2, Non-goals, alternative 5), ADR-0141's "Unchanged" line and `docs/design/marketplace-publishing.md` still describe the fold.** Answered with a recommendation to the seat: file it as a card when this PR merges. After the merge two accepted records disagree in their own text (ADR-0130 D2: "The consumer still installs one thing, opens one thing"), and a grep of the registry for D3 lands on "stand verbatim and unamended" with no pointer back. ADR-0141 set the precedent of adding the pointer lines to the records it re-read.
- **Spec prose that names the refused shape** (carrier #32586). Answered: each sentence stays true per package.

Flags this review adds:

- **The ruling's carrier is the card body**, written by a fleet seat from a session with the maintainer, verbatim and with its source. The amendment quotes it as "#32585 records it". This review cannot read that session. The PR is Tier H and the maintainer's own merge is the confirming act. No seat may stand in for it.
- **Landing state.** Draft, no auto-merge armed, no review requested by a seat. Nothing to disarm. The PR's author account is the fleet bot, so no separate author note is owed.

### ④ Design judgment

**`docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md`**

What holds, read against the tree:

- **The four ruled items.** Rule = card item 1. Vocabulary table = card item 3, four rows, `type: app` not renamed. Both rulings are quoted untranslated. The Status and Consequences lines of item 4 are rewritten with the old words still readable.
- **Reason 1.** `appRouteSegment` returns the package id, with the name only as a fallback. `matchAppBySegment` returns the first app that carries the id. The text above `appAddressSegment` says the name is the only address that reaches the others. `resolveAppPackageIdKey` returns the request unchanged when the package lists more than one app, so the read by package id finds nothing. ADR-0048 §3.1 states the route key on its "one-app-per-package invariant" in those words.
- **Reason 3.** `isDisableableAppModule` is true for a `type: module` package that directly declares an installed `type: app` package. `isItemOfDisabledPackage` judges an item by its own `_packageId`, and the list read and the by-name read both ask it.
- **"Enforced today, and not yet".** Accurate for `validateSingleApp` and for the `driver` pin.
- **The other records.** The quotations of ADR-0130 §1.5 and D2 and of ADR-0141 are accurate, and so are the two dates.
- **House style.** It matches the ADR-0093 D8 reversal on `main`: struck sentence, dated pointer, Amendment note blockquote, **Amended** status segment.
- **First consumer.** Three packages with one app each give three package ids and three distinct `/apps/PACKAGE_ID` routes. Composed with `manifest: 'preserve'` each app stays in its package body. Disabling the service or the marketing module removes that module's app, provided the module directly declares the app package. The amended D3 holds for that shape.

Findings:

**F1 · should-fix · reason 2 names one exception; the function it cites has two, and the second is the shape the reason's last sentence describes.**
`validateCrossReferences` returns at `if (objectNames.size === 0) return errors;` before it reaches the navigation walk. A package that defines no object is not judged for its app's `objectName` entries at all. The code names this leniency itself, in the docblock of `collectArtifactCrossReferenceErrors` ("An input declaring NO objects is skipped ... It is also why hotcrm#1449's measurement (an app package declaring no objects) never saw the defect"), and `stack.test.ts` pins the early return ("should skip cross-reference validation when no objects are defined"). Read from the code here, not run. Against it:

- "`defineStack` refuses an app's own navigation entry whose object its package does not define" holds only for a package that defines at least one object.
- "One measured exception" is short by one.
- "An app housed apart from its objects is a shell that only contributions can fill" is not true of a package that houses the app and no objects. That shell names any object in its own navigation and builds.

Why this is more than wording: the rule alone does not put an app with its objects. A module that holds only an app satisfies "at most one per package". Reasons 2 and 3 are what argue for housing an app with its objects, so the ADR should not say the build enforces more than it does. A later reader can also cite the bold sentence to close a leniency that is pinned and deliberate. The rule and the first consumer are not affected: by the card, each HotCRM package that holds an app holds objects.
Fix: state the precondition and the second exception in reason 2, and mark it read or probed, whichever the dev does.

**N1 · nit · D1 carries no dated pointer, though the note narrows one of its verbs.**
D1 says the thing a user "downloads, opens, and uninstalls is exactly one **App**". The vocabulary paragraph keeps "App" for what is "listed, installed and uninstalled (D1, D2, D4)" and says a suite may offer more than one app to open. So D1's "opens" no longer holds for a suite, while the status line, the revision history and the note each say "D1 ... unchanged". The card rules D1 unchanged for its listing clause, and the note reconciles the reading, so the contract is clear when the ADR is read whole. Context, D4 and Consequences each got a dated pointer; D1 read alone did not.

**N2 · nit, for #32586, not for this file · two shapes the Pending check, as the status line words it, would leave unjudged.**
The status line names "the `defineStack` check that holds a module package to at most one app". Reason 1 is about a package id, whatever produced it:

- A flat composition. `composeStacks` defaults to `manifest: 'last'` and concatenates `apps` under the one selected manifest. `validateSingleApp` has one caller, `defineStack`, and `os compile` parses the result with `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`. So two packages with one app each, composed without `preserve`, become one package with two apps that nothing refuses. Read from the code, not run.
- A package of the same artifact that is neither `app` nor `module`. ADR-0130 D2 names `plugin` beside `module`. The suite is defined as the app package plus its module packages, so the amended D3 neither lets such a package surface an app nor holds it to one.

Neither makes a sentence of the ADR wrong. Both are scope for the check's card to settle or to name as not decided.

Round: no must-fix. F1 is a should-fix: it is to be fixed before the PR is put to the maintainer, and its fix earns a delta review by this reviewer. The fix moves the head, and this review record covers `0df9c8b2` only. N1 may ride the same commit and the delta review reads it. N2 goes to #32586.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `82729d78f4773519a86752792c3c85db7ee97a4b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md + none

Delta review of record 6818867679, which judged head `0df9c8b2` (PASS, one should-fix F1, nits N1 and N2). This record judges the delta `0df9c8b2..82729d78` on the one file in scope. Every line of the file outside the delta is byte-identical to the text 6818867679 judged, so the two records together cover the file on this head.

Read for this review: card #32585 (body and its five comments), this PR's body and file list, the delta, the net diff against the merge base `8bfbc4ed` (+162 / -8, one file), and the 48 check-runs on the head. The cited code was read on `main` at `8bfbc4ed`. Every file the amendment cites is byte-identical there, at `874166b6` and on `main` today (`0f98e697`). Nothing was checked out, built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The merge brought nothing into the ADR file. Right.** `ba0523c7` has the parents `0df9c8b2` and `8bfbc4ed`. The file's blob at the merge commit is the blob at `0df9c8b2`, and `main` did not touch the file between the old merge base and `8bfbc4ed`. The merge commit differs from `8bfbc4ed` in this file alone, by the +137 / -7 the first record judged. The delta is the one commit `82729d78`, +39 / -15, in this file alone.
- **Accept-set of `@objectstack/spec`: unchanged. Right.** ADR prose only.
- **Nothing normative moves in the delta. Right.** The rule paragraph, the vocabulary table and the status line are untouched. The delta rewrites reason 2, adds a dated note under D1, strikes one label in D3's first sentence, and adds one sentence to the vocabulary paragraph and one to "Enforced today".
- **The index does not move. Right.** The status line is byte-identical to the one on `0df9c8b2`, and `docs/adr/README.md` on the head is the blob on `8bfbc4ed`.
- **One more symbol anchor**, eleven in all: `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts#collectArtifactCrossReferenceErrors`. The function exists on `main` under that name.

Gate verdicts are the check-runs on the head: 48 runs, 26 success, 22 skipped, none failed, none pending.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from 6818867679. Nothing in the diff publishes and the PR carries `skip-changeset`. On this head `Check Changeset` is skipped, which is the label's own exemption in `pr-automation.yml`. The title has no `!`.

`Clause-②: no` on the PR body is still right.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` in the dev's second report (card comment 6819201804) is empty. Its flags, each answered:

- **The PR body was not edited and is stale against this head.** Answered, and closed while this review ran: the body was still the first round's when the review began, and the seat has since replaced it. The body now on the PR was read. It agrees with the tree on this head in each place the report named: the head and the counts (+162 / -8, 181 lines to 335), the 风险 line of 维护者速读 (the precondition and both shapes), the D1 note and the struck label, and Acceptance notes 3 and 7. Nothing more is asked.
- **Card item 2 is no longer quoted word for word in reason 2.** Answered: sound. The unscoped sentences were false of a package that defines no object. What changed is a reason, not the rule of item 1. The maintainer is told: the replaced body says so in its 风险 line and in Acceptance note 3.
- **Written beyond F1: the strict-parse half of the precondition, and one sentence under "Enforced today".** Answered: both hold (④).
- **The label "(suite)" struck in place of an explanatory sentence.** Answered: sound (④), with nit N3.
- **The commit the note cites moved from `874166b6` to `8bfbc4ed`.** Answered: the cited files are byte-identical at both.
- **Out of scope, unchanged: ADR-0130, ADR-0141 and `docs/design/marketplace-publishing.md` still describe the fold.** The recommendation of 6818867679 stands: a card when this PR merges.

Carried from 6818867679 and unchanged: the HotCRM citations are unverified here and by the dev; the ruling's carrier is the card body and the maintainer's own merge confirms it; N2 is scope for #32586. Landing state on this head: draft, no auto-merge armed, no reviewer requested, author account the fleet bot.

### ④ Design judgment

**`docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md`, the delta**

**1. F1 is fixed.** Reason 2 now states its precondition, names both shapes that pass, and scopes its closing sentence. Each statement against `validateCrossReferences` and `buildDefinedStack` on `main`:

- "Under the strict parse, the default": `const strict = options?.strict !== false;`. Holds.
- "in a package that defines at least one object ... refuses an app's own navigation entry that names an object the package does not define": the walk refuses a `type: object` entry whose `objectName` is not among the stack's own objects. Holds. `type: object` is the only navigation entry that carries `objectName` (`app.zod.ts`), so no other entry type names an object past this check.
- "still refuses the entry when a sibling package of the same artifact defines that object": the walk reads the stack's own object names, never the artifact scope. Holds.
- "In a package that defines no object the check does not run" and "returns before it reads any navigation (read)": `if (objectNames.size === 0) return errors;` stands before the walk, and none of the ten collectors called ahead of it mentions navigation. Holds.
- "deliberate and pinned (read)": the quoted words are in the docblock of `collectArtifactCrossReferenceErrors`, and `stack.test.ts` pins the early return. Holds.
- "An entry that declares `requiresObject` is not judged": `if (!nav.requiresObject)`. Holds.
- The closing sentence, scoped to "a package that defines objects, but not the objects it shows", and "The build holds no more than that". Holds for what the reason is about, which is naming an object.

Every "(probed)" and "(read)" mark agrees with the code as read here. That a probe was run is the dev's statement (ten readings in 6819201804, each the answer the code gives by reading). This review ran none.

**2. N1 is fixed.** The note under D1 is in the form of the notes under Context and D4. It keeps D1's rule, keeps "downloads" and "uninstalls" on the one App that is the app package, keeps the listing clause, and says "opens" reads differently for a suite. That is what the vocabulary paragraph already said, now at D1.

**3. The struck "(suite)" and the vocabulary sentence are sound.** D3's heading says a suite may surface several apps, and its first sentence called the removed shape a suite. Striking the label removes that clash inside the decision section and deletes nothing: the sentence still stands per package, and the bullet under "What is reversed, and what stands" says where the word went. The vocabulary sentence is accurate for the four places it names. One place is missing, N3.

**4. What the delta newly asserts.**

- "Outside the strict parse nothing is judged: `strict: false` skips the pass": `buildDefinedStack` returns under `if (!strict)` before the schema parse, before `validateCrossReferences` and before `validateSingleApp`. "skips the pass" holds exactly. See N4 for "nothing".
- "The build does not require an app to sit in the package of the objects it shows. That placement is argued by reasons 2 and 3, not checked": holds. Both passing shapes house an app apart from the objects it names, and the rule of card item 1 asks for a different package per app, not for the package of the app's objects. This is the sentence F1 asked the ADR not to leave implied.
- "builds on `main` at `8bfbc4ed`": holds, `stack.zod.ts` is unchanged there.
- "Reason 2 marks each of its statements": every statement about what `defineStack` does is marked. The two citations of records and the description of the `requiresObject` key are not, and need not be.

Findings on the delta:

**N3 · nit · the vocabulary sentence's list of places is short by one.**
It names Context, Out of scope, Consequences and Alternatives 1 and 2 as where the accepted text uses "suite" in the earlier sense. D4's last sentence does too ("Folding a suite like HotCRM"), and D4 is a decision section. No reader is misled: the dated note right under D4 already says that sentence illustrates the fold D3 no longer requires. Accepted as it stands.

**N4 · nit · "nothing is judged" is one word broad.**
Under `strict: false` one refusal survives: `mergeActionsIntoObjects` refuses an `objects` value that is not an array, or an entry that is not an object, in both modes. It judges no reference and no app count, so the sentence holds for everything reason 2 and the single-app rule are about. Accepted as it stands.

Round: F1 and N1 are closed. No must-fix and no should-fix on the delta. Nits alone end the round. N3 and N4 are accepted deviations and no fix is asked; a fix would move the head off this record. N2 of the first record stays with #32586.
